Glossary of Embedded Linux & Yocto Terms ​

A comprehensive reference of all terminology used across the 16-Day Masterclass, sourced from official Yocto Project documentation.

A ​

Append File (.bbappend): A file that extends or overrides an existing recipe without modifying the original. Must match the recipe name (e.g., busybox_%.bbappend extends any version of busybox). See Day 16.

Autotools: The GNU build system (autoconf, automake, libtool) used by many open-source projects. In Yocto, use inherit autotools to automatically handle ./configure && make && make install. See Day 14.

B ​

BB_NUMBER_THREADS: Configuration variable in local.conf controlling how many BitBake tasks execute in parallel. Typically set to the number of CPU cores.

BitBake: The task execution engine at the heart of the Yocto build system. Written in Python, BitBake parses recipes, resolves dependency graphs, fetches source code, and orchestrates the entire build pipeline. See Day 1.

Board Support Package (BSP): A collection of metadata (machine configuration, kernel patches, bootloader recipes, device tree files) that enables Yocto to build images for a specific hardware platform. See Day 4.

Bootloader: The first software executed after CPU power-on reset. Initializes critical hardware (clocks, DRAM) and loads the Linux kernel. Common bootloaders: U-Boot, Barebox. See Day 3.

C ​

Class (.bbclass): A shared module of build logic that recipes can inherit using inherit <class>. Examples: autotools, cmake, core-image, kernel. See Day 14.

CMake: A cross-platform build system generator. In Yocto, use inherit cmake. See Day 14, Day 15.

Cross-Compiler: A compiler that runs on one architecture (host, e.g., x86_64) but generates binaries for a different architecture (target, e.g., ARM). See Day 1.

D ​

DEPENDS: Specifies build-time dependencies. Lists recipe names that must be built before the current recipe. Populates recipe-sysroot with headers and libraries. See Day 13.

DESTDIR / ${D}: The staging directory representing the target root filesystem. do_install copies files here, and do_package splits them into packages. See Day 8.

Device Tree Blob (.dtb): A binary data structure describing hardware peripherals (memory-mapped registers, interrupt assignments, bus topology) to the Linux kernel. Compiled from Device Tree Source (.dts) files using dtc. See Day 3.

Devshell: An interactive development shell launched with bitbake -c devshell <recipe>. Provides a terminal with all cross-compilation environment variables pre-set. See Day 15.

DL_DIR: The directory where BitBake stores downloaded source archives and git repositories. Defaults to build/downloads/. Can be shared across builds.

E ​

EXTRA_IMAGE_FEATURES: Set in conf/local.conf to inject image features across all local builds without modifying image recipes. See Day 7.

EXTRA_OECONF: Passes additional arguments to ./configure when using inherit autotools. See Day 14.

EXTRA_OECMAKE: Passes additional -D definitions to cmake when using inherit cmake. See Day 14.

F ​

FILESEXTRAPATHS: Extends the search path for local files referenced in SRC_URI. Critical for .bbappend files. See Day 16.

FILES:${PN}: Lists file patterns belonging to the main runtime package. Resolving [installed-vs-shipped] errors requires adding missing paths here. See Day 11.

I ​

IMAGE_FEATURES: A high-level variable enabling predefined feature sets in image recipes (e.g., ssh-server-dropbear, debug-tweaks, read-only-rootfs). See Day 7.

IMAGE_INSTALL: Lists packages to include in the root filesystem image. Use :append syntax to add packages. See Day 1.

L ​

Layer: A directory of related metadata (recipes, classes, configuration) that can be added to or removed from a build. Prefixed with meta- (e.g., meta-raspberrypi, meta-ti, meta-xilinx). See Day 2.

LIC_FILES_CHKSUM: A mandatory recipe variable containing the checksum of the software's license file. BitBake verifies this checksum to detect unintended license changes. See Day 8.

M ​

MACHINE: Defines the target hardware platform. Set in conf/local.conf. Examples: qemuarm, beaglebone-yocto, raspberrypi3, zedboard-zynq7. See Day 1.

Metadata: The collective term for all configuration files (.conf), recipes (.bb), appends (.bbappend), and classes (.bbclass).

O ​

oe_runmake: A Yocto helper function that executes make with cross-compilation variables automatically passed. See Day 9.

OpenEmbedded-Core (OE-Core): The core metadata layer (meta/) containing fundamental recipes, classes, and configuration for building embedded Linux. See Day 1.

P ​

PACKAGES: Variable listing all output packages generated by a recipe, in left-to-right priority order. See Day 11.

PARALLEL_MAKE: Sets the -j flag for make commands. Controls compilation parallelism within a single recipe.

Poky: The Yocto Project reference distribution combining BitBake + OE-Core + meta-poky + meta-yocto-bsp. See Day 1.

R ​

RDEPENDS: Specifies runtime dependencies. Lists package names that must be present on the target system. See Day 13.

Recipe (.bb): A file containing instructions for building a single software package. Defines where to fetch source code, how to compile it, and how to package the output. See Day 8.

Renode: An open-source hardware emulator supporting Zynq-7000/ZedBoard and other platforms. See Renode Guide.

Root Filesystem (rootfs): The complete directory hierarchy (/bin, /etc, /lib, /usr) that Linux mounts as / after booting. See Day 1.

S ​

Shared State Cache (sstate-cache): A directory storing compiled build artifacts keyed by input hash. Allows BitBake to skip rebuilding unchanged recipes, dramatically reducing build times. See Day 2.

SOLIBS / SOLIBSDEV: Variables controlling how versioned (.so.1.0) and unversioned (.so) shared libraries are assigned to packages. See Day 12.

SRC_URI: Specifies the location(s) of source code, patches, and local files for a recipe. Supports http://, git://, file://, and other fetcher protocols. See Day 8.

SRCREV: Specifies the exact Git commit hash to checkout. Ensures reproducible builds. See Day 10.

T ​

Toolchain: The cross-compiler, binutils, C library, and kernel headers used to compile software for the target architecture. See Day 1.

W ​

WIC (.wic): A tool and disk image format that creates pre-partitioned, bootable SD card images. Configured via .wks (kickstart) files. See Day 4.

WORKDIR: The temporary build directory for a recipe under tmp/work/<arch>/<pn>/<pv>/. Contains fetched sources, build outputs, and task logs. See Day 8.
